theorem: For V=V_(1,1) of SU(3), dim 8, the marginal Phi_27 of Gamma_27(X)=(4/27)P_27[(X tensor I)+(I tensor X)]P_27 is symmetric-compatible. On End(V_8)=1+8_s+8_a+10+10bar+27 its exact multipliers are (1,14/25,2/3,28/75,28/75,218/675). In normalized-trace Hilbert-Schmidt order on the full operator space, every full-domain EB comparator E satisfying I-E<=C(I-Phi_27) requires C>=2. One full-domain SU(3)-orbit EB channel attains C=2 on the full space, so the unrestricted-EB optimum is exactly 2. It also satisfies (I-E)^2<=2(I-Phi_27).
quantifiers: The compatible marginal and carrier are fixed; E ranges over all EB CPTP maps M_8->M_8, not merely covariant or orbit maps. If E is not Hilbert-Schmidt selfadjoint, the order is interpreted through its symmetric part. The comparison covers every operator sector for this fixed channel, not a channel sequence or the dimension-free bounded-Holevo implication.
proof_or_counterexample: Twirling any comparator preserves the full quadratic-form inequality and makes it covariant and bistochastic; symmetrize with its EB Hilbert-Schmidt adjoint if needed. Every covariant separable Choi state is a convex mixture of twirled pure product seeds. For each pure seed, ||q_a||^2<=1/24 sharply, so every such EB channel has anti-copy coefficient at most 1/3. Since Phi_27 has anti-copy coefficient 2/3, C>=2. The root seed gives multipliers (1,1/5,1/3,1/15,1/15,7/135); exact sector projection norms show I-E<=2(I-Phi_27) on all sectors, with equality on 8_a. As 0<=I-E<=I, the squared comparison follows. The full tracial score-family consequence is T<=0.5 sqrt(2 theta r).

quantifiers: Every fixed a in (0,1); the commuting family uses m equal basis blocks, while the Clifford family uses m pairwise anticommuting Hermitian Pauli matrices. The common measurement is one pure-state reference ensemble shared across all family states.
proof_or_counterexample: The commuting diagonal signs have a common basis measurement capturing all variance. In the Clifford frame H_x=(a/sqrt(m)) sum_i x_i Gamma_i, anticommutation gives H_x^2=a^2 I and the uniform covariance has flat rank-m spectrum. For every pure state, sum_i <Gamma_i>^2<=1; an eigenbasis of Gamma_1 attains equality, hence the best common POVM captures exactly a^2/m and Delta=a^2(1-1/m). The established compatible commutator inequality gives residual r>=a(1-1/m)/(2+sqrt(2))^2, so this is not a small-broadcast-error counterexample.

theorem: For a state family E, a certified trace-distance epsbar-net R of N rational density matrices, and a supplied full-domain CPTP broadcaster B with measured net marginal error beta_R, define Gamma(R)=max_p (sum_i sqrt(p_i))^2 chi_p. Then e_EB(E)<=min{1,2 epsbar+inf_K[phi(K) beta_R+sqrt(Gamma(R)/(2K))]}, with phi(K)=s+2-2^(s+1)/K for 2^s<=K<=2^(s+1), phi(1)=0. Also Gamma(R)<=N C(R)<=N lnN.
quantifiers: The cover certificate bounds every member of E by epsbar from some net state. The broadcaster is one physical full-domain CPTP map with arbitrary correlated outputs. The resulting EB decoder is common to all states and labels. Measured beta_R is max over both marginals and all net states.
proof_or_counterexample: Iterate B over a minimum-average-depth K-leaf binary tree and permute the outputs, costing K-1 calls and mean depth phi(K). For each prior, sequential history-dependent Helstrom tests yield a posterior trace-spread bound through classical Pinsker, Bayes contraction of (sum sqrt(p))^2, and the Holevo information chain. Preparing the posterior mean state after a suitable prefix gives a prior-specific EB map; finite-dimensional minimax supplies one common decoder. Compare each conditional decoder state to the conditional remaining-receiver state, then average the latter over histories before using the net broadcast error. Finally trace contraction extends the decoder from R to E.
